title: Slay the Spire 2 Teases a Hidden Spire Area and Its Floating Mystery Creature
excerpt: Mega Crit's September Neowsletter teases a new Slay the Spire 2 area with a floating creature silhouette and asks fans for fan art guesses by October 8.
content:
Barcelona was the setting for the Slay the Spire 2 team’s break, and Mega Crit came home with a new mystery in tow. The September 2026 Neowsletter, posted Friday, September 25, says the studio is rested and back at work. It also shows a silhouette of a creature from a part of the Spire nobody has seen yet.

The team describes the trip in relaxed terms.

“We visited the historied city of Barcelona and ate all the tapas, walked through all the Gaudís, and navigated its winding gothic quarters for silly trinkets.” – Slay the Spire 2 on Steam

The newsletter admits it arrived later than usual and will be on the smaller side. The team says it is still easing back into its groove.

A New Corner of the Spire Is Still in the Dark

The real news is the returning Spire Spotting segment. Mega Crit says its researchers have found another area of the Spire that is still shrouded in darkness. The only proof so far is the outline of one of its inhabitants.

That matters for the world before it matters for the deck. The Spire has been the whole stage since the first game, and a new region means new residents with their own reasons for being there. Mega Crit hasn’t said who this creature is, what it wants, or whether it will help or hurt you.

The studio’s own description is short.

“Interesting… it appears to be some sort of small, floating, excitable being. Though this isn’t the most scientific of descriptors, it seems almost… cute!” – Slay the Spire 2 on Steam

“Almost cute” is a fun choice of words in a game where cute things tend to have teeth. Take it as a hint at tone, not a promise.

What Mega Crit Wants From You by October 8

The segment is a call for fan art. Mega Crit asks players to submit their artistic guesses at the creature’s true form. Send them to [email protected] or post them in the fanart channel on the studio’s Discord. The deadline is Thursday, October 8.

That is the same day New York Comic Con opens. Mana Wave will have a booth there from October 8-11 with a limited edition Ironclad variant of a Slay the Spire item. The Steam post cuts off before naming the exact item.

The Next Patch Has No Date Yet

Mega Crit gave no timeline or specifics for the next patch. What it did say is that the work in progress is big, and that much of it is already being tested internally. The list of what the team has resumed is broad: secret features, game modes, content, bug fixes and quality of life improvements.

The game itself is still in Early Access. It launched on Steam on March 5, 2026, and is currently listed at $24.99. Steam shows the overall user rating as Mixed across 202,462 reviews, as of September 26, 2026.

Early Access Players Are Split on Balance

That Mixed rating is a useful backdrop, because the most helpful reviews we checked lean the other way. Of the 20 most-helpful reviews sampled, 16 were positive and 4 were negative. So the sample is friendlier than the overall score, and you shouldn’t read either quote below as the final word.

The positive side is about the pull of one more run. This reviewer had 41 hours in when they wrote it during early access:

“I play this game the same way the old lady keeps pulling on the slot machine hoping for something different to happen this time I also can’t stop but atleast they don’t charge me per spin” – ARIANARCHY, 41 hours played

The negative side is about balance, and Mega Crit says balance and bug fixes are part of the work it has resumed. This review came from a player with 45 hours, also written during early access:

“Balancing needs a lot of work. For some characters the build almost doesn’t matter, you won’t make it past the third boss. Until that is fixed, it’s really more of a frustration simulator. StS1 did a much better job here” – North, 45 hours played

The newsletter doesn’t say which fixes are in the next patch, so nobody can tie that complaint to a specific change yet. What it does give is one new silhouette and a firm date to draw toward. The guesses are due Thursday, October 8.
